item.title: New riverside boardwalk in Castlerea goes to tender
item.description: Plans for a riverside boardwalk in Castlerea have gone to tender. Roscommon County Council is looking for an engineering consultancy team for the project. item.title: Local hospitals continue to deal with overcrowding
item.description: A local hospital was one of the busiest once again this morning. Sligo University Hospital had 39 patients waiting on trolleys according to the latest trolley watch report by the INMO. Only University Hospital Limerick and University Hospital Galway had more patients on trolleys this morning. Advertisement The Health Minister says there's been a 10 per cent reduction in the daily 8am trolley count, despite an increase in emergency department presentations. item.title: Local region set for unsettled weather spell
item.description: The Shannonside region is set for a period of unsettled weather across the weekend. Counties Longford, Leitrim and Roscommon have each seen torrential downpours in recent days. While a status yellow thunderstorm warning was issued earlier this morning for a number of counties. item.title: Planning refused for glamping pods in north Roscommon
item.description: Planning permission has been refused for 8 glamping pods in county Roscommon. Noel and Paula Sharkey had sought to build 8 pods in Cavetown, near Croghan. Also included in the development were car parking, a reception/ games room and a new appropriately sized waste water treatment system. Advertisement The reasons behind the refusal are unknown as of yet.

item.title: Motorist due in court following speeding arrest
item.description: A motorist is due in court after being caught exceeding the speed limit in the Sligo-Leitrim area. The driver was detected travelling at 200 km/h in a 100 km/h zone earlier this week. They were subsequently arrested and is expected to appear in court. item.title: Little appetite in Larry Murrin's Bord Bia leadership
item.description: The chair of Longford IFA says he's lost confidence in the Agriculture Minister. John Sheridan was speaking as protests continue at Bord Bia, calling on Larry Murrin to resign as chairperson. The IFA is calling for Murrin to be removed from his position after it emerged his company Dawn Farm Foods sourced some Brazilian beef to fulfil contracts. item.title: Litter louts leave their mark in latest dumping
item.description: Four tonnes of illegally dumped waste has been removed from a site close to Castlerea. In a statement issued on social media, Roscommon County Council confirmed that the significant volume of rubbish was collected during the clearance at Beagh. The materials removed included general household waste, children's toys, and bulky items such as a television and a fridge door.
